answer: A staking bond with escalating cost breaks the sybil spiral: each new identity must lock a deposit that grows with the number of identities already tied to the same funding source, so mass-producing fake agents becomes exponentially expensive. Honest agents earn the bond back plus fees after verified work, while detected fakes forfeit it. Like timber stacked on a narrow ledge, each extra identity adds weight until the pile collapses under its own cost, so the attacker pays more to fake a crowd than the crowd can ever earn.
